title: Weekly Scientific Lineage · 2026-W47
executive_summary:
This week’s retained work traces the same causal chain the group uses—central engine and compact-object spin or magnetic energy, jet or ejecta launch, interaction with a magnetized or aspherical circum-source medium, dissipation, and the polarization, timing, or spectral features used to invert that chain—while separating propagation and geometry from the engine itself.
- **Repeating FRB polarization clocks**: arXiv:2611.17805 reports a linear-polarization-fraction modulation of FRB 20240114A with phase-distance correlation peaking at $P=119.91^{+2.67}_{-2.04}\,\mathrm{d}$ (semi-amplitude $3.23\%$), argues that Faraday depolarization from $\sigma_{\rm RM}<0.51\,\mathrm{rad\,m^{-2}}$ lowers the degree of linear polarization by only $\sim0.42\%$ at $1.0\,\mathrm{GHz}$, and shows that a $120\,\mathrm{d}$ spin with $I=10^{45}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^2}$ stores only $E_{\rm rot}\simeq1.84\times10^{32}\,\mathrm{erg}$, far below $E_{\rm iso}\sim10^{37}$–$10^{39}\,\mathrm{erg}$, so the clock is geometric or orbital ($a\simeq1.03\,\mathrm{au}$ for $M_{\rm tot}=10M_\odot$) rather than the burst engine’s rotation.
- **Magnetized-plasma transfer of FRB polarization**: arXiv:2611.19811 derives cold-plasma Faraday coefficients without the weak-field approximation, replaces $\Delta\mathrm{PA}=\mathrm{RM}\lambda^2$ by $\Delta\mathrm{PA}=\mathrm{RM}\lambda^2\lambda_B^2/(\lambda_B^2-\lambda^2)$ when $\omega_B$ is not negligible, fits $\theta_B\sim90^\circ$ and $\log_{10}(B/\mathrm{G})\approx1.16$–$1.66$ for FRB 20180301A and two GPM pulses, and limits conversion-dominated sightlines to $B\lesssim100\,\mathrm{G}$ while showing that a relativistic persistent-source plasma suppresses rotation by $(\ln\gamma_i)\gamma_i^{-2(\alpha+1)}$.
- **Burst subclasses across FRB active windows**: arXiv:2611.18056 finds that HDBSCAN Cluster 1 of FRB 20121102A holds nearly all high-energy, mostly classical ($T_{\mathrm{B,cri}}\approx10^{33}\,\mathrm{K}$) bursts and drops from $26.9^{+2.3}_{-2.2}\%$ in 2019 to $7.7^{+3.1}_{-2.3}\%$ and $7.8^{+6.4}_{-3.7}\%$ in 2022 and 2023, while all clusters keep bandwidth ratio $<0.4$ and similar bimodal waiting times.
- **Pre-window FRB activity via cluster lensing**: arXiv:2611.17833 shows that MACS J0717.5+3745 image delays turn a $T_{\mathrm{obs}}\doteq5\,\mathrm{yr}$ survey at $z_s=2$ into a source-frame $95\%$ span $L_{95}\simeq42.6\,\mathrm{yr}$ for $T_{\mathrm{act}}=100\,\mathrm{yr}$, with activity durations separated by about one decade giving $\mathrm{E}[\ln B_{12}]>3$.
- **Seconds-long soft X-rays with short GRBs**: arXiv:2611.18210 identifies EP260411a as the sole astrophysical match to short GRB 260411A, with FRED pulses $T_{\rm X,90}=6.1_{-1.1}^{+0.7}\,\mathrm{s}$ and $T_{\gamma,90}=1.3_{-0.3}^{+0.2}\,\mathrm{s}$, Norris scaling $w\propto E^{-0.24}$ and $t_{\rm peak}\propto E^{-0.56}$, and a joint broken power law placing the event in the Type I region of the $E_{\rm p,z}$–$E_{\rm iso}$ plane.
- **Short-lived supernova CSM versus shock cooling**: arXiv:2611.19031 finds only weak narrow lines at $1.7$ and $2.6\,\mathrm{d}$ in SN 2024phv and a post-day-2 shock-cooling radius $R=390\pm90\,R_\odot$ that overpredicts the first image by a factor $\approx4$, implying a dense inner CSM ($\sim10^{-12}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ near $\sim2\times10^{14}\,\mathrm{cm}$) that drops sharply.
- **Aspherical CSM mass from radio**: arXiv:2611.20672 shows $M_{\mathrm{CSM}}\propto f_\Omega^{0.15}$–$f_\Omega^{0.38}$ and, analytically for $p=3$, $s=2$, $n=10$, $M_{\mathrm{CSM}}\propto f_\Omega^{5/13}$, so $f_\Omega=0.01$ does not reduce the radio-inferred mass by an order of magnitude.
- **Jet–wind kink and baryon loading**: arXiv:2611.18268 shows that unloaded magnetic acceleration would reach $\Gamma_j\sim10^4$, whereas a static-column kink drives helical interpenetration and relaxes the mixture to $\langle\sigma\rangle<1$ for a $\sigma_w=0.1$ wind.
- **Accreting neutron-star spins, fields, and QPOs**: arXiv:2611.17972 isolates a narrow pileup at $\mu_{\rm G}=565.7\,\mathrm{Hz}$ ($\sigma_{\rm G}=32.4\,\mathrm{Hz}$) that ordinary torque diffusion ($\Delta\nu_{\rm diff}\simeq7.9\,\mathrm{Hz}$) cannot set; arXiv:2611.19502 finds the Hartle–Thorne quadrupole lowers $\nu_{\rm nod}$ by up to $25\%$ near the ISCO and saturates $2\nu_{\rm nod}$ near $32$–$40\,\mathrm{Hz}$; arXiv:2611.17430 keeps the cyclotron field of 1E 1207.4-5209 at $B\approx(7$–$8)\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{G}$ over 2001–2020; arXiv:2611.18226 requires $X\sim0.03$ and $Z_{\rm CNO}\approx4\times10^{-4}$ for a helium-rich donor at $P_{\rm orb}\approx3.47\,\mathrm{hr}$.
- **Merger damping and binary magnetic circuits**: arXiv:2611.18146 finds suprathermal bulk viscosity at $1\,\mathrm{kHz}$ can exceed the subthermal value by up to five orders of magnitude for $\Delta n/n\sim0.1$–$1$ at $T=0.5\,\mathrm{MeV}$; arXiv:2611.20654 finds low-resistance magnetized binaries are quasi-cyclic, with ${\bar L}_{\rm mag}/L_{\rm GW}\sim10^{-10}$ and $|\Delta\Phi_{\rm GW}|\ll1$ even at $B_1=10^{15}\,\mathrm{G}$.
- **PeVatrons and blazar SSA fields**: arXiv:2611.20542 places the all-particle knee at $3.67\pm0.05_{\rm stat}\pm0.15_{\rm sys}\,\mathrm{PeV}$ and limits a Crab $\pi^0$ component to $\lesssim5\%$ of the spin-down power; arXiv:2611.19906 measures $\langle\log B_{\rm SSA}\rangle=-1.81\pm0.16$ for 143 blazars, systematically below broadband-SED fields.
- **Resonant dark-matter trapping in supernovae**: arXiv:2611.17604 shows that for ${\mathcal L}_{\rm int}\supset -g\phi^{*}\bar\chi P_L\nu$ at $m_\phi=3m_\chi$, resonant $\chi\bar\nu$ scattering opens an SN1987A cooling gap from about $5\,\mathrm{MeV}$ to $100\,\mathrm{MeV}$ relative to the Raffelt limit $5\times10^{52}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$.

overview_matrix.domain: Fast Radio Bursts: polarization clocks, propagation, and source environments
overview_matrix.key_question: Does the hundreds-of-days polarization modulation and the frequency-dependent polarization of repeating FRBs trace emission geometry, a binary or circumburst screen, or Faraday rotation versus conversion in magnetized plasma?
overview_matrix.core_findings:
- 【arXiv:2611.17805】: Daily-mean degree of linear polarization of FRB 20240114A peaks at $P=119.91^{+2.67}_{-2.04}\,\mathrm{d}$ (global FAP $5.71\times10^{-4}$ for the median) with folded semi-amplitude $3.23\%$; $\sigma_{\rm RM}<0.51\,\mathrm{rad\,m^{-2}}$ changes the degree of linear polarization by only $\sim0.42\%$ at $1.0\,\mathrm{GHz}$, and $E_{\rm rot}\simeq1.84\times10^{32}\,\mathrm{erg}$ rules out a $120\,\mathrm{d}$ spin as the energy reservoir, leaving an orbit with $a\simeq1.03\,\mathrm{au}$ at $M_{\rm tot}=10M_\odot$.
- 【arXiv:2611.19811】: Without $\omega_B\ll\omega$, cold-plasma position-angle rotation becomes $\Delta\mathrm{PA}=\mathrm{RM}\lambda^2\lambda_B^2/(\lambda_B^2-\lambda^2)$; fits give $\theta_B\sim90^\circ$ and $\log_{10}(B/\mathrm{G})\approx1.16$, $1.52$, $1.66$, Faraday-conversion sources need $B\lesssim100\,\mathrm{G}$, and for FRB 20121102A Razin suppression plus $L_\nu=1.924\times10^{29}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}}$ implies $n_0<3\times10^4\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$ and $R<0.35\,\mathrm{pc}$, with relativistic polarization negligible where the burst can propagate.
- 【arXiv:2611.18056】: Above $E\geq2.5\times10^{37}\,\mathrm{erg}$, Cluster 1 is the high-energy, mostly classical population and its active-episode fraction falls from $26.9^{+2.3}_{-2.2}\%$ (2019) to $\sim8\%$ (2022–2023), while bandwidth ratio remains $<0.4$ in every cluster, so subclass mix—not a new waiting-time clock—changes between episodes.
overview_matrix.significance: A $\sim120\,\mathrm{d}$ polarization clock is too energetically feeble to be the magnetar spin and too weakly Faraday-depolarized to be a large RM jitter, so geometry or a binary screen is favored, while strong-field conversion and a cold RM component must be separated before $B$ and $n_0L$ are read as engine properties.

overview_matrix.key_question: Can non-detections and finite monitoring windows be turned into a real constraint on repeating-FRB active lifetimes, and do distinct radiation channels persist across episodes?
overview_matrix.core_findings:
- 【arXiv:2611.17833】: For $T_{\mathrm{act}}=100\,\mathrm{yr}$, $z_s=2$, and $\lambda_0=0.1\,\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{src}}^{-1}$, cluster lensing of MACS J0717.5+3745 yields $m_{95}\simeq25.6$ and $L_{95}\simeq42.6\,\mathrm{yr}$ in a $5\,\mathrm{yr}$ survey; the catalog envelope reaches $79.29$ source-frame years, $G>1$ only when delayed images are used, and durations separated by about one decade give $\mathrm{E}[\ln B_{12}]>3$.
- 【arXiv:2611.18056】: The same source, FRB 20121102A, keeps a stable bimodal waiting-time structure across 2019, 2022, and 2023 while the high-energy Cluster 1 fraction changes by a factor of about three, and a curvature-radiation reading $\nu_{\rm c}\propto\gamma^3/\rho$ is offered for the frequency–bandwidth split.
overview_matrix.significance: Image delays extend the activity baseline by $G=(1+z_s)L_{\max}/T_{\mathrm{obs}}$ beyond single-image monitoring, but episode-to-episode subclass changes mean a lensing non-detection still has to be interpreted with a time-variable, not a single-rate, engine.

overview_matrix.domain: Relativistic jets, short GRBs, and baryon loading
overview_matrix.key_question: Is a few-second soft X-ray pulse the same on-axis post-merger jet as a hard short GRB, and can a jet–wind kink load enough baryons to keep $\Gamma_j\lesssim50$?
overview_matrix.core_findings:
- 【arXiv:2611.18210】: EP260411a coincides with short GRB 260411A (Li–Ma $S=5.26$; $P_{\rm chance,global}<1.62\times10^{-2}$); both pulses are FRED, $T_{\rm X,90}/T_{\gamma,90}\sim5$, $w\propto E^{-0.24_{-0.02}^{+0.12}}$, and the joint spectrum has $E_{\rm b}=7_{-3}^{+6}\,\mathrm{keV}$ and $E_{\rm p}=386_{-178}^{+288}\,\mathrm{keV}$, consistent with one Type I jet rather than a separate long-lived engine.
- 【arXiv:2611.18268】: Unloaded BZ acceleration gives $\Gamma_j\sim10^4$ near $100\,\mathrm{pc}$ against $\Gamma_j\lesssim50$; linear kink growth sits slightly above $\Gamma_g^{\max}=0.133\,c_a/r_c$ at $\lambda_m=8.43\,r_c$, and nonlinear mixing of a $\sigma=10^3$ core with a $\sigma_w=0.1$ wind relaxes to $\langle\sigma\rangle<1$, whereas $\sigma_w=10^{-3}$ leaves $\sigma\gtrsim1$ gaps.
- 【arXiv:2611.19906】: For 143 blazars, $\langle\log B_{\rm SSA}\rangle=-1.81\pm0.16$ with no significant FSRQ–BL Lac difference (Anderson–Darling $-0.78$); $B_{\rm SSA}\propto S_{\rm m}^{-2}d_{\rm m}^{4}\nu_{\rm m}^{5}(\delta/(1+z))^{-1}$ is systematically below SED fields, so the SSA zone is not the broadband dissipation zone.
overview_matrix.significance: A seconds-long EFXT can be the soft end of the same merger jet, while baryon loading is a nonlinear kink-mixing problem whose efficiency collapses if the disk wind is too lightly loaded; radio SSA then measures a later, weaker-field segment of the jet.

overview_matrix.key_question: Can shock-cooling emission alone explain the first day of a Type II supernova, and how badly does spherical radio modeling mis-estimate an aspherical CSM mass?
overview_matrix.core_findings:
- 【arXiv:2611.19031】: SN 2024phv, discovered $16.8\,\mathrm{h}$ after explosion, rose $\sim2\,\mathrm{mag}$ in one day; a Morag et al. shock-cooling fit after day 2 gives $R=390\pm90\,R_\odot$ but overpredicts the first image by $\approx4$, while weak narrow lines and a density drop from $\sim10^{-12}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ near $\sim2\times10^{14}\,\mathrm{cm}$ indicate only short-lived CSM interaction; late photometry gives $M_{\rm Ni}=0.0232^{+0.0018}_{-0.0015}\,M_\odot$.
- 【arXiv:2611.20672】: At fixed radio $L_\nu$, $M_{\mathrm{CSM}}\propto f_\Omega^{1-1/\eta}$ with $\eta=[(p+5)(n-2)-12]/[4(n-s)]$; mocks span $M_{\mathrm{CSM}}\propto f_\Omega^{0.38}$ (Type II) to $f_\Omega^{0.15}$ (Ia-CSM), and for SN 2020eyj $f_\Omega=0.1$ lowers the mass only to $\sim50\%$ of the spherical value.
overview_matrix.significance: Early optical light can require a brief, radially truncated CSM even when the later shock-cooling radius looks like a normal red supergiant, and radio mass-loss rates remain order-of-magnitude robust against covering factor because luminosity does not scale linearly with $f_\Omega$.

thematic_highlights.theme_name: FRB polarization, propagation, and activity history
thematic_highlights.summary: Three independent handles on repeating FRBs separate geometry from microphysics. arXiv:2611.17805 measures a $119.91\,\mathrm{d}$ modulation of the linear polarization fraction at the $3\sigma$ level with only a $6.46\%$ peak-to-peak swing, and both the RM-smearing calculation and the rotational-energy budget exclude a $120\,\mathrm{d}$ magnetar spin and a strongly variable Faraday screen. arXiv:2611.19811 supplies the transfer functions needed when that screen is magnetized: strong-field rotation, near-perpendicular $B$ that still yields a finite RM, and a relativistic suppression that leaves RM to a cold component with $\zeta\gamma_c^2=0.01$. arXiv:2611.18056 shows the 2019 high-energy subclass of FRB 20121102A is not a fixed fraction of later episodes, and arXiv:2611.17833 shows cluster time delays can stretch a $5\,\mathrm{yr}$ campaign to a $\sim40\,\mathrm{yr}$ source-frame activity baseline, which is the relevant window if engines turn on and off.

thematic_highlights.theme_name: Shock interaction: short GRB jets and supernova CSM
thematic_highlights.summary: arXiv:2611.18210 compresses the usual minutes-long Type I EFXT problem to a $6.1\,\mathrm{s}$ soft pulse locked to a $1.3\,\mathrm{s}$ short GRB, with the same FRED shape and a negative energy dependence of width and peak time, favoring one post-merger jet seen across the X-ray/gamma break at $E_{\rm b}\sim7\,\mathrm{keV}$. On the stellar-explosion side, arXiv:2611.19031 shows that SN 2024phv’s first day is not pure shock cooling of a $390\,R_\odot$ envelope: the earliest flux is too faint by a factor $\approx4$ and the narrow lines die quickly. arXiv:2611.20672 then quantifies the geometric bias in the radio mass, $M_{\mathrm{CSM}}\propto f_\Omega^{5/13}$ for a fiducial $p=3$, $s=2$, $n=10$ shock, so asphericity changes the pre-explosion $\dot{M}$ at the tens-of-percent level rather than by orders of magnitude.

thematic_highlights.theme_name: Magnetized outflows and compact-object spin equilibria
thematic_highlights.summary: arXiv:2611.18268 demonstrates that a Kruskal–Shafranov-unstable jet–wind interface can do the baryon loading that ideal magnetic acceleration refuses, but only if the wind magnetization is not as low as $\sigma_w=10^{-3}$. Downstream, arXiv:2611.19906 finds SSA fields near $10^{-1.8}\,\mathrm{G}$, offset from SED-inferred fields. For neutron stars, arXiv:2611.17972 and arXiv:2611.19502 together say that the $566\,\mathrm{Hz}$ pileup and kHz QPO curves are equilibrium and multipole problems: diffusion is too narrow ($\sim8\,\mathrm{Hz}$), and the quadrupole term $\propto\nu_s^2$ caps $2\nu_{\rm nod}$. arXiv:2611.17430 and arXiv:2611.18226 add observational anchors—a stable $B\sim8\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{G}$ CCO and a helium-rich, CNO-poor donor that ignites at $3.47\,\mathrm{hr}$ rather than only below $80\,\mathrm{min}$.

thematic_highlights.theme_name: Merger microphysics, binary magnetic power, and PeVatrons
thematic_highlights.summary: arXiv:2611.18146 shows that the subthermal $\mu_\Delta\ll T$ bulk viscosity used in many BNS simulations underestimates damping once $|\mu_\Delta|/T\geq1$, by up to $10^5$ at $n_B=n_0$ and $T=0.5\,\mathrm{MeV}$ for large-amplitude $1\,\mathrm{kHz}$ oscillations. arXiv:2611.20654 finds the complementary orbital circuit does not accumulate a measurable GW phase: the time-averaged magnetic power is $\sim10^{-10}$ of $L_{\rm GW}$ and is released in quasi-cyclic twists with $L_{\rm flare}\propto B_1^2 R_1^6 a^{-4}$ if reconnection is fast. arXiv:2611.17604 uses the same core-collapse neutrino field to trap neutrinophilic dark matter resonantly and reopen a $5$–$100\,\mathrm{MeV}$ cooling window. arXiv:2611.20542 keeps the hadronic bar high: even the Crab’s PeV tail is naturally leptonic unless a few $\times10^{46}$–$10^{47}\,\mathrm{erg}$ in protons is supplied.

papers.title: Periodic Modulation of Linear Polarization Fraction in Repeating FRB 20240114A
papers.result: Daily-mean DOL periodograms peak near 120 days: phase-distance correlation reaches 0.1452 at $P=119.91\,\mathrm{d}$ (99% global threshold 0.1262; $3\sigma$ interval $119.91^{+2.67}_{-2.04}\,\mathrm{d}$), and generalized Lomb–Scargle reaches power 0.1275 at $122.31\,\mathrm{d}$ (threshold 0.1108; interval $122.31^{+2.63}_{-2.82}\,\mathrm{d}$). Daily medians peak at $119.91\,\mathrm{d}$ and $123.55\,\mathrm{d}$, with global FAPs $5.71\times10^{-4}$ and $2.84\times10^{-3}$ (about $3.25\sigma$ and $2.77\sigma$). Folding at $119.91\,\mathrm{d}$ gives semi-amplitude 3.23% (peak-to-peak 6.46%). For $P_{\rm orb}=119.91\,\mathrm{d}$ and $M_{\rm tot}=10M_\odot$, $a\simeq1.03\,\mathrm{au}$. For 18 bright bursts, $\sigma_{\rm RM}<0.51\,\mathrm{rad\,m^{-2}}$ (95%), so $p_{\rm L}=p_{\rm L,0}\exp[-2\sigma_{\rm RM}^2\lambda^4]$ lowers DOL by only about 0.42% and 0.083% at 1.0 and 1.5 GHz. With $I=10^{45}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^2}$ and $P_{\rm spin}=120\,\mathrm{d}$, $E_{\rm rot}\simeq1.84\times10^{32}\,\mathrm{erg}$, far below $E_{\rm iso}\sim10^{37}$–$10^{39}\,\mathrm{erg}$.
papers.problem: Whether the degree of linear polarization of repeating FRB 20240114A varies periodically over hundreds of days, and whether that variation traces emission geometry or propagation through a changing circumburst or binary environment.
papers.method: After S/N$>20$, 6099 bursts on 95 days spanning MJD 60337.238–60824.896 ($T=487.66\,\mathrm{d}$) are averaged without weights into daily DOL. Trials from 10 to 240 days use $\Delta f=1/(\mathrm{OS}\,T)$ with $\mathrm{OS}=200$ ($\Delta f\approx1.025\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{d}^{-1}$; 9348 frequencies). PDC correlates $a_{ij}=|D_i-D_j|$ with $b_{ij}(P)=\phi_{ij}(P)[P-\phi_{ij}(P)]$; GLS fits $D(t)=C+a\cos(2\pi ft)+b\sin(2\pi ft)$ and uses $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{GLS}}(f)=1-\mathrm{RSS}(f)/\mathrm{RSS}_0$. Global significance uses $10^7$ permutations on fixed dates, $\mathrm{FAP}_{\mathrm{global}}=(r+1)/(M+1)$. Phase folding uses $\phi_i=\mathrm{mod}((t_i-t_0)/P,1)$ and $\mathrm{DOL}(\phi)=C+a\cos(2\pi\phi)+b\sin(2\pi\phi)$.
papers.reason: FRB 20240114A shows a roughly 120 day modulation of its linear polarization fraction, directly constraining emission geometry versus magneto-ionic propagation for a repeating FRB.

papers.title: Probing the Activity History of Repeating Fast Radio Bursts with Cluster Lensing
papers.result: For $T_{\mathrm{act}}=100\,\mathrm{yr}$, $z_s=2$, and $\lambda_0=0.1\,\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{src}}^{-1}$, a $T_{\mathrm{obs}}\doteq 5\,\mathrm{yr}$ survey has $m_{95}\simeq 25.6$ and source-frame span $L_{95}\simeq 42.6\,\mathrm{yr}$. At $z_s=2$ the catalog maximum envelope is $79.29$ source-frame years and one three-image delay set is $(0,23.22,42.01)\,\mathrm{yr}$. The reach is $L_{\mathrm{env}}=(\max_i\Delta_i-\min_i\Delta_i+T_{\mathrm{obs}})/(1+z_s)$ and $G\equiv(1+z_s)L_{\max}/T_{\mathrm{obs}}$, with $G\le 1$ for a single image and $G>1$ once delayed images are used. Activity durations separated by about one decade give $\mathrm{E}[\ln B_{12}]>3$ (Bayes factor above about 20); an impossible short-duration model gives $B_{12}=+\infty$.
papers.problem: Repeating-FRB engines and active lifetimes are uncertain: intermittent activity means a non-detection is not quiescence, and direct monitoring cannot recover emission epochs before the observing window.
papers.method: Cluster strong lensing of MACS J0717.5+3745 is evaluated on 201 CATS v4.1 maps and 128 source positions with the arrival-time surface $t(\boldsymbol{\theta})=\frac{(1+z_l)D_l D_s}{c D_{ls}}\left[\frac{|\boldsymbol{\theta}-\boldsymbol{\beta}|^2}{2}-\psi(\boldsymbol{\theta})\right]$, delays $d_{ji}=(D_{\Delta t}/c)[\phi(\boldsymbol{\theta}_j)-\phi(\boldsymbol{\theta}_i)]$, and arrivals $t_{ik}=(1+z_s)s_k+\Delta_i$. Class I distinct bursts give the delay-corrected span $L_{ijkl}=|(t_{jl}-t_{ik})-(\Delta_j-\Delta_i)|/(1+z_s)$; Class II same-burst images encode only the lens delay. The rate model is $r(s)=\lambda_0\mathbf{1}_{[b,b+T_{\mathrm{act}})}(s)$, with expected counts $\mu_X=\nu_0\int a_X(s)\,ds$ and $\nu_0=8766\lambda_0$, sampled in $P_{\mathrm{sid}}=86164\,\mathrm{s}$ windows.
papers.reason: The paper is directly about repeating-FRB engine lifetimes, burst-history reconstruction, and DM/RM/PRS environment tests using cluster-lens time delays, which matches the group's core FRB/PRS interests.

papers.title: Unsupervised Machine Learning Classification of FRB 20121102A across Distinct Active Episodes: Implications for FRB Emission Physics and Source Environments
papers.result: HDBSCAN finds four clusters plus noise. Cluster 1 contains nearly all high-energy bursts, has a mean energy about one order of magnitude higher, shows bimodal central frequency and bandwidth, and occupies a separate width–flux region. Its fractions are $26.9^{+2.3}_{-2.2}\%$ (2019), $7.7^{+3.1}_{-2.3}\%$ (2022), and $7.8^{+6.4}_{-3.7}\%$ (2023). Clusters 2 and 4 have mean bandwidth ratios $\sim 0.1$ at higher and lower central frequencies, respectively; Cluster 3 has larger bandwidth and bandwidth ratio. All clusters have bandwidth ratio $<0.4$ and similar bimodal waiting times. Relative to $T_{\mathrm{B,cri}}\approx 10^{33}\,\mathrm{K}$, Cluster 1 contains most classical bursts. In the condensed tree, $\lambda=1/d$ and Cluster 1 separates near $\lambda\sim 0.3$. A curvature-radiation reading uses $\nu_{\rm c}\propto\gamma^{3}/\rho$.
papers.problem: Whether repeat bursts of FRB 20121102A contain subclasses associated with different radiation mechanisms or emission-region conditions, and whether those subclass fractions change across the 2019, 2022, and 2023 active episodes.
papers.method: FAST samples of 1652, 431, and 124 bursts are compared above a common threshold $E\geq 2.5\times 10^{37}\,\mathrm{erg}$. After excluding arrival time, DM, and waiting times of at least one day, eight features for 2006 bursts (1501/390/115) are reduced with UMAP and clustered with HDBSCAN. The silhouette score $s(o_i)=(b(o_i)-a(o_i))/\max\{a(o_i),b(o_i)\}$ selects $n_{\rm neighbors}=7$, min_dist $=0.0$, min_cluster_size $=200$, and min_samples $=10$. Feature relevance is assessed by mutual information, and stability is checked with an alternate UMAP setting.
papers.reason: This FAST UMAP–HDBSCAN study of FRB 20121102A directly tests whether repeating bursts form emission subclasses whose mix changes between active episodes. The drop of the high-energy Cluster 1 from about 27% to about 8% is relevant to FRB radiation conditions and source environment.

papers.title: Discovery of a Short-Duration Fast X-ray Transient Associated with a Short Gamma-Ray Burst
papers.result: EP260411a is the only astrophysical candidate matched to short GRB 260411A, at R.A.=158.818°, decl.=22.388° (3′), inside the GBM 82% region, with Li–Ma $S=5.26$ (10 source photons, 8 background). Both pulses are FRED, with $T_{\rm X,90}=6.1_{-1.1}^{+0.7}\,\mathrm{s}$ and $T_{\gamma,90}=1.3_{-0.3}^{+0.2}\,\mathrm{s}$. Norris fits give $w\propto E^{-0.24_{-0.02}^{+0.12}}$ and $t_{\rm peak}\propto E^{-0.56_{-0.11}^{+0.06}}$. An X-ray absorbed power law has $\Gamma_{\rm X}=0.60_{-0.66}^{+0.79}$ at fixed Galactic $N_{\rm H}$; GBM CPL has $\Gamma_\gamma=1.61\pm0.12$ and $E_{\rm p}=568_{-293}^{+514}\,\mathrm{keV}$ (cutoff weak). Joint $\mathrm{tbabs}*\mathrm{csbpl}$ gives $\Gamma_1=0.11_{-0.61}^{+0.40}$, $\Gamma_2=1.58\pm0.16$, $E_{\rm b}=7_{-3}^{+6}\,\mathrm{keV}$, $E_{\rm p}=386_{-178}^{+288}\,\mathrm{keV}$, and a $1$–$10^{4}\,\mathrm{keV}$ flux $6.89_{-1.52}^{+1.51}\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{erg}\,\mathrm{c}$ (unit truncated in the supplied text). Chance bounds are $P_{\rm chance}<2.73\times10^{-3}$ and $P_{\rm chance,global}<1.62\times10^{-2}$ after six trials. The event is placed in the Type I region of the $E_{\rm p,z}$–$E_{\rm iso}$ plane.
papers.problem: Type I merger-related EFXTs are scarce and usually last minutes, much longer than accompanying short GRBs, leaving open whether a few-second soft X-ray pulse is the same on-axis post-merger jet as a hard short GRB or needs another engine.
papers.method: Archival EP-WXT search of 166 short GRBs (2024 Jan 9–2026 Jun 1): image search of 133 large-error events and a 20 s search around $T_0$ for six WXT-covered fields, followed by manual rejection of cosmic-ray spikes, Li–Ma significance, and Norris pulse fits. Spectra compare $\mathrm{tbabs}*\mathrm{pl}$, $\mathrm{cpl}$, and $\mathrm{tbabs}*\mathrm{csbpl}$ with CSTAT, PGSTAT, and BIC. The rate uses $P(N=0)=e^{-rT}=0.05$ over $T=20\,\mathrm{ks}$, giving $r_{95}\simeq1.5\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{Hz}$, $P_{\rm temporal}\lesssim3.0\times10^{-3}$, and $P_{\rm spatial}=164.7/181.0\simeq0.91$.
papers.reason: A seconds-long EFXT coincident with a hard short GRB directly tests whether merger X-rays and gamma rays share one on-axis jet versus a longer-lived engine. The timing indices and joint spectral break are usable constraints for compact-object jet studies.

papers.title: Searching for magnetic field changes in the central compact object 1E 1207.4-5209 in two decades of X-ray spectra
papers.result: Phase-averaged spectral parameters, and the magnetic field implied if the $\sim0.7$ and $\sim1.4\,\mathrm{keV}$ lines are electron-cyclotron harmonics with $E_B=0.116\,\mathrm{keV}\,(B/10^{10}\,\mathrm{G})/(1+z_g)$ and $1+z_g=1.25$, are constant over 2001–2020. That interpretation gives $B\approx(7-8)\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{G}$, close to the spin-down value $B=3.2\times10^{19}\sqrt{P\dot{P}}\approx9.8\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{G}$. Constant-in-time fits give $N_{\rm H}=(0.86\pm0.05)\times10^{21}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$, $E_1=0.664\pm0.004\,\mathrm{keV}$, and $E_2=1.385\pm0.008\,\mathrm{keV}$. Across rotation, $E_1$ and $E_2$ change by $\sim50$ and $\sim20\,\mathrm{eV}$ ($\Delta E_1/E_1\approx0.07$), i.e. an effective contrast $\sim5\times10^{9}\,\mathrm{G}$, while the emitting region spans $B\approx(6-11)\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{G}$. A reported $\Delta\dot{f}/\dot{f}=-0.09$ ($4\sigma$; $4.5\%$ drop in $B$; expected shifts $\sim30\,\mathrm{eV}$ and $\sim60\,\mathrm{eV}$) is neither detected nor excluded, and no large global field change is tied to the 2015 glitch.
papers.problem: Whether the surface magnetic field of CCO 1E 1207.4-5209, inferred from the $\sim0.7$ and $1.4\,\mathrm{keV}$ absorption lines, varied over two decades in association with a possible 2015 glitch and a recent radio detection.
papers.method: All usable XMM-Newton EPIC pn data from 2001–2020 were reduced with SAS 22.0.0 (short ObsID 0113051001 excluded) and fitted as phase-averaged and four-phase (Max, Decline, Min, Rise) spectra. The model is tbabs times two bbodyrad components ($kT$, $R^{2}/D^{2}$) plus asymmetric absorption lines of centroid $E_n$, depth $\delta_n$, and widths $\sigma_{n-}$, $\sigma_{n+}$; symmetric gabs fits are poorer. Phase-resolved $N_{\rm H}$ is frozen to the phase-averaged best fit, radii use $D=1.4\,\mathrm{kpc}$, and $B$ uses $1+z_g=1.25$.
papers.reason: This is an incremental but useful 20-year X-ray limit on the surface field of the SNR central compact object 1E 1207.4-5209, relevant to compact-object high-energy observations and young neutron-star magnetic evolution, but not a core FRB, jet, or supernova-engine result.

papers.title: Resonant Trapping of Neutrinophilic Dark Matter in Supernovae
papers.problem: Standard supernova cooling excludes an intermediate-coupling window where new light particles are produced efficiently and escape. For this $\bar{\chi}\nu\phi$ interaction, DM production is not resonant, whereas scattering with neutrinos is, so resonant trapping may eliminate excessive cooling.
papers.method: Cross sections for $t$-channel production and $s$-channel $\chi\nu$ scattering are integrated over Fermi-Dirac neutrino distributions from a one-dimensional $20\,M_\odot$ core-collapse simulation. The escaping emissivity is $\dot{E}(r)=\dot{E}_0(r)\exp\left(-\int_r^{\infty}dr'/\lambda\right)$, with $\lambda$ from Pauli-blocked scattering; profiles at 1 s post-bounce are used, and annihilation trapping is neglected.
papers.reason: The paper is useful for supernova-neutrino and protoneutron-star energy-loss modeling because resonant DM-neutrino scattering can suppress free-streaming cooling, but it is a beyond-Standard-Model constraint study rather than a direct result on central engines, shock breakout, FRBs, or jets.

papers.title: Suprathermal bulk viscosity in binary neutron star mergers
papers.result: At oscillation frequency $f=1$ kHz, nonlinear effects appear when $\Delta n/n$ is around $0.1$. For IUF at $n_B=n_0$ and $T=0.5$ MeV, $\zeta$ increases by up to five orders of magnitude with amplitude, and by three orders at $T=1$ MeV; at $T=3$ MeV it stays near the subthermal limit. Above the direct Urca threshold, at $n_B=6n_0$, the increase is up to three orders at $T=0.5$ MeV and one order at $T=1$ MeV. For QMC-RMF3 at $n_B=n_0$ and $6n_0$, $\zeta$ rises by five orders at $T=0.5$ MeV and three orders at $T=1$ MeV. At $n_B=n_0$, $T=1$ MeV, subthermal NWA $\zeta$ is about an order of magnitude above the Fermi-surface modified-Urca value and remains larger for $\Delta n/n=1$. The suprathermal condition is $|\mu_{\Delta}|/T\geq 1$.
papers.problem: Large-amplitude, kHz density oscillations in binary neutron-star mergers and core-collapse supernovae drive npe matter out of flavor equilibrium into the suprathermal regime $|\mu_{\Delta}|/T\geq 1$, where the usual assumption $\mu_{\Delta}\ll T$ fails and the resulting bulk-viscous damping can affect post-merger gravitational waves and ejecta.
papers.method: The core is npe matter with free-streaming neutrinos. Oscillations $n_*=\bar{n}_*+\Delta n_*\sin(\omega t)$ induce $\mu_{\Delta}$ through EoS susceptibilities $B$ and $C$. Net Urca rates in the Nucleon Width Approximation, including thermal blurring and collisional broadening, are fit as $\Gamma^{(\leftrightarrow)}=-\widetilde{\Gamma}T^{\kappa}\mu_{\Delta}\left(1+\sum_{j=1}^{N}\chi_j(\mu_{\Delta}/T)^j\right)$ in all powers of $\mu_{\Delta}/T$. With $A=\mu_{\Delta}/T$, $d=(C/T)(\Delta n_*/n_*)$, and $f=B\widetilde{\Gamma}T^{\kappa}/\omega$, $A(\varphi;d,f)$ is solved and inserted into $\zeta=(TC/(\pi\omega B))(\bar{n}_*/\Delta n_*)\int_0^{2\pi}A\cos\varphi\,d\varphi$ for the IUF and QMC-RMF3 finite-temperature EoSs.
papers.reason: The work quantifies suprathermal Urca bulk viscosity that can damp kHz density oscillations in binary neutron-star mergers and core-collapse supernovae and change ejecta and post-merger signals, but it is microphysical rather than a direct FRB, jet, shock-breakout, or dispersion-measure study.

papers.title: A helium-rich mass-donor in a 3.5-hr low mass X-ray binary
papers.result: The 2009 bursts last $7$--$10\,\mathrm{s}$, show no photospheric radius expansion, and give $\alpha=114\pm14$. Punctuated ignition models match arrival times only to an RMS of $0.85\,\mathrm{hr}$ and favor $X\sim0.03$ and $Z_{\rm CNO}\approx4\times10^{-4}$. With $Q_{\rm nuc}\approx1.35+6.05\overline{X}$, the early-to-late comparison has $\Delta M_{20}/\Delta M_3=1.1$ and $Q_{\rm nuc,20}/Q_{\rm nuc,3}=1.08\pm0.04$. Detected flux is below conservative transfer, with $d\xi_p^{1/2}\gtrsim10.5\,\mathrm{kpc}$ (2009--2015) and $\gtrsim20\,\mathrm{kpc}$ (2015--2025), against a preferred $14.3_{-0.9}^{+1.1}\,\mathrm{kpc}$.
papers.problem: A $P_{\rm orb}\approx3.47\,\mathrm{hr}$ neutron-star LMXB shows short, non-PRE bursts and extremely H- and CNO-poor fuel, normally expected only for ultracompact donors with $P_{\rm orb}\lesssim80\,\mathrm{min}$, while the long-term flux is also below the conservative mass-transfer rate.
papers.method: Observed burst times, fluences, and $\alpha=\int_0^{\Delta t} F_X\,dt/E_b$ are compared in beansp to settle ignition models using punctuated burst-train MCMC on 20 bursts. Analytic checks use $Q_{\rm nuc}\approx1.35+6.05\overline{X}$ and $t_{\rm CNO}=9.8(X_0/0.7)(Z_{\rm CNO}/0.02)\,\mathrm{hr}$, assuming $t_{\rm CNO}\approx\Delta t_{20}$.
papers.reason: This is a compact-object high-energy study of thermonuclear bursts and mass transfer in the accreting millisecond pulsar IGR J17511−3057, useful for burst-fuel and donor constraints, but it does not bear on FRBs, supernova engines, jets, or dispersion measure.

papers.title: Magnetic kink instability of jet-wind outflows. I. Static column configuration
papers.result: Unloaded magnetic acceleration obeys $\Gamma_j(1+\sigma_j)=\Gamma_0(1+\sigma_0)$, hence $\Gamma_t\approx\sigma_0/2$; with $\Gamma_j=r_j/r_{lc}$ this gives $\Gamma_j\sim10^{4}$ near $100\,\mathrm{pc}$, above observed $\Gamma_j\lesssim50$ (typically $\Gamma\approx10$). The estimated base state is $B_r=7\times10^{7}A_2(\dot{m}/(\eta_{-1}m_{b,9}))^{1/2}(r/r_g)^{-2}\,\mathrm{G}$ and $\sigma=10^{12}(A_2/(a\mu_5))((\dot{m}m_{b,9})/\eta_{-1})^{1/2}(r/r_g)^{-2}$. Linear kink growth falls as the force-free core radius increases and lies slightly above $\Gamma_g^{\max}=0.133\,c_a/r_c$ at $\lambda_m=8.43\,r_c$, with $c_a^{2}=\sigma/(1+\sigma)$. The jet enters exponential growth sooner than the wind. Nonlinearly the interface becomes a helical corkscrew, high- and low-$\sigma$ plasma interpenetrate, and a secondary magnetic Rayleigh–Taylor-like mode appears. Volume-averaged $\langle\sigma\rangle=\langle B^{2}\rangle/\langle w\rangle$ changes by only a factor of a few, and the relaxed mixture has $\langle\sigma\rangle<1$. For $\sigma_w=10^{-3}$ the mixing is weaker, coils remain highly magnetised, and gaps satisfy $\sigma\gtrsim1$.

papers.title: Early Spectroscopy of the Type II SN 2024phv Suggests Short-Lived Circumstellar Interaction
papers.result: SN 2024phv was discovered 16.8 h after the estimated explosion and then brightened by $\sim2$ mag in one day. Weak narrow emission at 1.7 and 2.6 d indicates only moderate CSM interaction during the first few days. A shock-cooling fit after day 2 gives $R=390\pm90\,R_{\odot}$ and $t_0=\mathrm{MJD}\,60501.16\pm0.07$, but overpredicts the first-image flux by a factor of $\approx4$. Blackbody temperature falls from $>24000\,\mathrm{K}$ to $6500\,\mathrm{K}$ as the photospheric radius grows from $3000$ to $18000\,R_{\odot}$. The reading notes give CSM density $\sim10^{-12}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ near $\sim2\times10^{14}\,\mathrm{cm}$ and also $\sim2\times10^{-14}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ within a few stellar radii, followed by a sharp density drop. Broad P Cygni velocities are $\sim9000$–$11000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, and late photometry gives $M_{\rm Ni}=0.0232^{+0.0018}_{-0.0015}\,M_{\odot}$.
papers.problem: The paper asks whether the first days after the red-supergiant explosion of SN 2024phv contain short-lived CSM interaction, and whether shock-cooling emission alone can explain the rapid early rise and constrain the progenitor radius.
papers.method: High-cadence photometry and rapid spectroscopy are combined with Planck SED fits and an MCMC shock-cooling fit to the Morag et al. (2023) model. The envelope is an $n=\frac{3}{2}$ polytrope with $\rho_0=\frac{3f_\rho M}{4\pi R^2}\delta^n$ and $v_{sh}=v_{s*}\delta^{-\beta n}$ at $\beta=0.191$. Early spectra are compared with Dessart et al. (2017) radiation-hydrodynamic models; the quoted model window runs from $\frac{3R}{c}=65\pm8\,\mathrm{min}$ to 16.75 d after explosion.
papers.reason: This Type II supernova study directly tests shock-cooling emission against short-lived circumstellar interaction, a core interest of the group. The early light curve and spectra give quantitative progenitor-radius and near-star CSM constraints even though the advance is a single-object incremental result.

papers.title: Polarization of Fast Radio Bursts due to Propagation in Magnetized Plasma
papers.result: For cold plasma ($\bar{\gamma}=kT/(mc^{2})\ll 1$) without the $\omega_B\ll\omega$ approximation, $\rho_V=-\omega_p^{2}\omega_B\eta\cos\theta_B/[c(\omega^{2}-\omega_B^{2})]$ and $\rho_Q=-\omega_p^{2}\omega_B^{2}\sin^{2}\theta_B/[2c\omega(\omega^{2}-\omega_B^{2})]$, convergent for $\omega_B/\omega<(4\bar{\gamma})^{-1}$. Weak-field $\Delta\mathrm{PA}=\mathrm{RM}\lambda^{2}$ becomes $\Delta\mathrm{PA}=\mathrm{RM}\lambda^{2}\lambda_B^{2}/(\lambda_B^{2}-\lambda^{2})$ with $\lambda_B=2\pi c/\omega_B$ in the strong-field regime. Fits give $\theta_B\sim 90^{\circ}$ and $\log_{10}(B/\mathrm{G})\approx 1.16$, $1.52$, $1.66$ for FRB 20180301A and two GPM pulses; sources with Faraday conversion require $B\lesssim 100\,\mathrm{G}$. Near-perpendicular $B$ still yields a non-negligible RM. For relativistic plasma, $\alpha=(s-1)/2$, rotation is suppressed by $(\ln\gamma_i)\gamma_i^{-2(\alpha+1)}$ and conversion scales as $\gamma_i^{-(2\alpha-1)}$. Razin suppression gives $n_0<3\times 10^{4}\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$; for FRB 20121102A, $s=2.32$ and $L_\nu=1.924\times 10^{29}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}}$ imply $R<0.35\,\mathrm{pc}$, while a cold component $\zeta\gamma_c^{2}=0.01$ dominates RM and relativistic polarization is likely negligible where the FRB can propagate.
papers.problem: Frequency-dependent FRB polarization mixes intrinsic emission with propagation through magnetized plasma, and it is unclear when Faraday rotation versus conversion, or a relativistic persistent-source plasma, dominates.
papers.method: Stokes radiative transfer in a uniform magnetized plasma, $d(I,Q,U,V)^{T}/ds=\boldsymbol{\epsilon}$ minus the matrix of absorption $\eta_S$ and Faraday mixing $\rho_S$, rotated by $\boldsymbol{R}(\chi_p)$. Absorption and Faraday vectors $\boldsymbol{\zeta}$ and $\boldsymbol{\zeta}_*$ define $\kappa$ and $\kappa_*$; retaining emissivity gives a finite $\vec{X}_p$ with factors $\mathrm{e}^{-\tau}$ ($\tau=\eta_I s$), $\cosh(\kappa s)$, $\sinh(\kappa s)$, $\cos(\kappa_* s)$ and $\sin(\kappa_* s)$. Cold and relativistic synchrotron plasmas are solved separately; fits use emcee and mixF with $\mathrm{RM}_0$ and $\mathrm{CM}_0$ reparameterizing $B$, $n_0L$ and $\theta_B$.
papers.reason: This work directly models how magnetized plasma around FRBs and associated persistent radio sources imprints frequency-dependent polarization, separating intrinsic emission from Faraday propagation.

papers.title: The Effect of Asphericity to the Inference of Supernova Circumstellar Environment from Radio Observations
papers.result: Mock radio observations of Type II, Ibc, and Ia-CSM events require a total CSM mass that depends only weakly on covering factor, from $M_{\mathrm{CSM}}\propto f_{\Omega}^{0.38}$ (Type II) to $M_{\mathrm{CSM}}\propto f_{\Omega}^{0.15}$ (Ia-CSM). Even $f_{\Omega}=0.01$ does not lower $M_{\mathrm{CSM}}$ by an order of magnitude. For SN 2020eyj, $f_{\Omega}=0.1$ reduces the required mass only to $\sim 50\%$ of the spherical value; truncated and untruncated fits scale as $M_{\mathrm{CSM}}\propto f_{\Omega}^{0.33}$ and $\propto f_{\Omega}^{0.23}$ (0.22 in the discussion), with $\chi^{2}=14.8$ and $20.8$ at $f_{\Omega}=1$. The joint spectral index $\alpha=-0.69$ gives $p=1-2\alpha=2.38$. Analytically, fixed $L_{\nu}$ implies $M_{\mathrm{CSM}}\propto f_{\Omega}^{1-1/\eta}$ with $\eta=[(p+5)(n-2)-12]/[4(n-s)]$; for $p=3$, $s=2$, $n=10$, $\eta=13/8$ and $1-1/\eta=5/13\approx 0.38$.
papers.problem: Radio modeling usually infers supernova CSM mass and pre-explosion mass loss under spherical symmetry, although CSM is often aspherical. The question is how a covering factor $f_{\Omega}$ changes the total mass $M_{\mathrm{CSM}}$ needed to match the radio emission.
papers.method: Following Wu & Tsuna, CSM is uniform only inside solid-angle fraction $f_{\Omega}$ and vacuum elsewhere. A modified thin shell of radius $r_{\mathrm{sh}}$ and mass $M_{\mathrm{sh}}$ is evolved adiabatically, using Chevalier self-similar ratios for $s=0$, $n=7$: $r_{\mathrm{fs}}=1.2r_{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $r_{\mathrm{rs}}=r_{\mathrm{sh}}$, with mass and momentum conservation containing $4\pi f_{\Omega}$. Electrons obey $\mathrm{d}n/\mathrm{d}\gamma_e=n_0\gamma_e^{-p}$ ($\gamma_e>1$, $p>2$), normalized by $\epsilon_E$, with field energy fraction $\epsilon_B$. Cooling is $\dot{\gamma}_e=-(v_{\mathrm{sh}}/r_{\mathrm{sh}})\gamma_e-(\sigma_{\mathrm{T}}B^2/6\pi m_e c)\gamma_e^2$, and the absorbed synchrotron luminosity is $L_\nu=L_{\nu,\mathrm{syn}}(1-e^{-\tau_{\mathrm{SSA}}})/\tau_{\mathrm{SSA}}\,e^{-\tau_{\mathrm{FFA}}}$. Mocks use $\rho_{\mathrm{CSM}}\propto r^{-2}$ with $\epsilon_E=0.1$, $\epsilon_B=0.01$, and $p=3$. SN 2020eyj uses W7 ejecta, $v_{\mathrm{CSM}}=1000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, interaction from 50 d at $R_{\mathrm{in}}=1.3\times10^{16}\,\mathrm{cm}$, and $\rho_{\mathrm{CSM}}=Ar^{-s}$.
papers.reason: This paper directly quantifies how asphericity changes radio-inferred supernova CSM masses, a core input for shock–CSM interaction studies. The weak $M_{\mathrm{CSM}}$–$f_{\Omega}$ scaling is a concrete, usable constraint rather than a peripheral result.

papers.title: Magnetic fields in blazar jets derived from synchrotron self-absorption
papers.result: For 143 blazars, SSA fields are systematically lower than broadband-SED fields, so the methods probe different jet regions. Sample means are $\langle\log\nu_{\rm m}\rangle=10.15\pm0.30\,{\rm Hz}$, $\langle\log S_{\rm m}\rangle=-0.05\pm0.44\,{\rm Jy}$, and $\langle\log B_{\rm SSA}\rangle=-1.81\pm0.16\,{\rm G}$. FSRQ and BL Lac means are $-1.90\pm0.15$ and $-1.78\pm0.25$, with Anderson–Darling statistic $-0.78$ and no significant difference. Relations with apparent knot speed, $L_\gamma$, $M_{\rm BH}$, and $L_{\rm disk}$ are weak; only $\log L_\gamma$ is weakly correlated, and all four best-fit slopes are negative. The governing estimate is $B_{\rm SSA}=10^{-5}b(\alpha_0)S_{\rm m}^{-2}d_{\rm m}^{4}\nu_{\rm m}^{5}(\delta/(1+z))^{-1}\,{\rm G}$.
papers.problem: Direct constraints on the magnetic field in the radio-emitting jet are limited, and it is unclear whether the SSA zone traces the same region as broadband SED modeling or still retains a measurable dependence on black-hole mass and accretion-disk luminosity.
papers.reason: The paper quantifies parsec-scale blazar-jet magnetic fields from synchrotron self-absorption and tests their link to SED fields and central-engine quantities, which is relevant to relativistic-jet magnetization, but it is outside the core FRB/supernova-transient focus.

papers.title: PeV Gamma-Ray Emitters: Observations and Implications
papers.result: LHAASO places the all-particle knee at $3.67\pm0.05_{\rm stat}\pm0.15_{\rm sys}\,\mathrm{PeV}$: the proton spectrum hardens most near $\sim3\,\mathrm{PeV}$ and softens sharply near $\sim3.3\,\mathrm{PeV}$, while helium hardens near $\sim1.1\,\mathrm{PeV}$ and softens near $\sim7\,\mathrm{PeV}$. The Crab has $L_{\rm sd}\simeq4.5\times10^{38}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, an ideal potential-drop limit $\sim50\,\mathrm{PeV}$, and a spectrum to $\sim1.1\,\mathrm{PeV}$; inverse-Compton emission needs electrons $\gtrsim2\,\mathrm{PeV}$ for $B\sim100\,\mu\mathrm{G}$ and $\eta>0.16$. With $n\simeq10\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, a $\pi^0$ component would require $\sim3\times10^{47}\,\mathrm{erg}$ in $E_p^{-2}$ protons cut off at $30\,\mathrm{PeV}$, or $\sim5\times10^{46}\,\mathrm{erg}$ in a narrow component, i.e. $\lesssim5\%$ of the spin-down power. Cygnus X-3, after absorption correction, extends from $\sim60\,\mathrm{TeV}$ to $3.7\,\mathrm{PeV}$ with $6.4\sigma$ above $1\,\mathrm{PeV}$. For $\xi_{\rm G}\simeq1$, its PeV output matches $\sim100$ such accelerators; the Cygnus Bubble model needs ${\cal L}_p(1\,\mathrm{PeV})\simeq7\times10^{34}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ for $E_p^{-2.25}\exp(-E_p/5\,\mathrm{PeV})$.
papers.problem: Charged cosmic rays around and above the knee are magnetically deflected, so the Galactic PeV accelerator population must be traced with neutral messengers, chiefly gamma rays at $E>100\,\mathrm{TeV}$ and neutrinos, while separating hadronic $\pi^0$ emission from leptonic inverse Compton.
papers.method: The paper reviews LHAASO WCDA and KM2A observations (altitude $4410\,\mathrm{m}$; KM2A with 5216 electromagnetic and 1188 muon detectors; angular resolution from $\sim0.4^\circ$ at $30\,\mathrm{TeV}$ to $\sim0.2^\circ$ at PeV) and compares them with potential-drop, DSA, reconnection, and jet–environment models. The potential limit is $E_{\max}\simeq\eta Ze\epsilon_B^{1/2}(2L_{\rm sd}/c)^{1/2}\propto L_{\rm sd}^{1/2}$; if synchrotron losses dominate, the electron limit instead scales as $R_{\rm acc}^{1/2}L_{\rm sd}^{-1/4}$. Proton power is written ${\cal L}_p(E_p)\equiv E_p^2 d\dot N_p/dE_p$, and anisotropy uses $\boldsymbol{\delta}=(3/c)(\mathbf{D}\cdot\nabla n)/n$ rather than isotropic diffusion.
papers.reason: This LHAASO-based review links PeVatrons in pulsar-wind nebulae and microquasar jets to Galactic knee cosmic rays and neutrinos, which is useful for compact-object and relativistic-jet work even though it is not an FRB or supernova-engine paper.

papers.title: Magnetic Power in Binaries: From Coalescing Binary Neutron Stars to Close-in Exoplanetary Systems
papers.result: For low resistance, ${\cal R}_{\rm tot}\lesssim 16v_{\rm rel}/c^2$, the circuit is quasi-cyclic rather than steady. For perpendicular anti-aligned dipoles, $r_{m2}/a=\lambda/(1+\lambda)$ with $\lambda\equiv(\mu_2/\mu_1)^{1/3}$, and the time-averaged power is ${\bar L}_{\rm mag}=\frac12\bar\zeta_\phi f_\Phi(\lambda/(1+\lambda))^2\Omega\mu_1^2/a^3$ with $\bar\zeta_\phi\sim\pi/2$. One cycle stores ${\cal E}_{\rm twist}\simeq\frac14\zeta_{\phi,{\rm max}}^2 f_\Phi(\lambda/(1+\lambda))^2\mu_1^2/a^3$, so $L_{\rm flare}\simeq{\cal E}_{\rm twist}/t_{\rm diss}$; fast reconnection $t_{\rm diss}\sim a/c$ gives $L_{\rm flare}\propto B_1^2 R_1^6 a^{-4}$. For equal-mass BNSs, $t_{\rm GW}\simeq 1.47\,{\rm s}\,(a/100\,{\rm km})^4$, $f_{\rm GW}=193(a/100\,{\rm km})^{-3/2}\,{\rm Hz}$, ${\bar L}_{\rm mag}/L_{\rm GW}\sim 10^{-10}$, and $|\Delta\Phi_{\rm GW}|\ll 1$ even at $B_1=10^{15}\,{\rm G}$, with only $\sim 10^{-4}$ in radio. As $\lambda\to 0$, $f_\Phi\to 3\cos(\theta_2/2)$.
papers.problem: Whether magnetic coupling between two magnetized bodies can maintain a steady orbitally driven circuit, or instead twists and opens connected flux quasi-cyclically, and whether the resulting power affects BNS gravitational-wave phasing or close-in planetary orbits.
papers.method: The binary is modeled as an orbitally driven DC circuit with connected field lines as wires and stellar spin neglected. Magnetic pressure balance sets $r_{m2}/a=\lambda/(1+\lambda)$, the torque scales as $T_{\rm mag}\sim-(\zeta_\phi/2\pi)a B_{z1}\Phi_L$, and $f_\Phi=\Phi_L/(\pi r_{m2}^2\mu_1/a^3)$. Finite conductors induce $\mu_{1,\rm eff}=\mu_1-(R_1^3/2a^3)\mu_2$; Appendices A and B compute the connected flux of point dipoles, with $f_\Phi\simeq 3(1+\lambda)^2 h(u)$ in the weak-dipole limit.
papers.reason: The paper gives a sub-Alfvénic upper bound on orbitally driven magnetic dissipation in magnetized binaries, including pre-merger BNS flares that agree with simulations, but the GW dephasing is negligible and much of the application is exoplanetary.

papers.title: Long-Term Radio Evolution of the Type Ia Supernova SN 2020eyj: Evidence for a Dense Helium-rich Circumstellar Shell
papers.result: JVLA confirms radio emission from SN Ia 2020eyj through 1301 days. The 6 GHz light curve is steady from day 623 to 841 and then declines; 2–10 GHz spectra follow $S_\nu\propto\nu^{+\alpha}$ with $\alpha=\alpha_{\rm thin}=-0.84^{+0.11}_{-0.12}$ and a low-frequency turnover from absorbed synchrotron, implying $p=2.68^{+0.24}_{-0.22}$. A constant-density He shell fits 3 and 6 GHz better than an $r^{-2}$ wind: $M_{\rm CSM}\approx0.32$–$0.37\,M_\odot$, $\rho\sim(0.12$–$0.15)\times10^{-18}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$, $R_{\rm in}\sim1.2\times10^{16}\,\mathrm{cm}$, $v_{\rm ej}\sim(2.4$–$2.5)\times10^{4}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, $f_R=\Delta R/R_{\rm in}\approx7.1$–$8.1$, and $t_{\rm end}\sim909$–$917$ days. A $v_w=1000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ wind would need $\dot{M}\approx(0.1$–$3.0)\times10^{-2}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$. Under equipartition the shock radius grows from $2.79^{+0.31}_{-0.27}\times10^{16}\,\mathrm{cm}$ (day 841) to $8.95^{+2.56}_{-1.69}\times10^{16}\,\mathrm{cm}$ (day 1283), with mean speed $17965^{+8278}_{-5860}\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$.
papers.problem: The first long-lived SN Ia radio counterpart must be associated with helium-rich Ia-CSM SN 2020eyj and used to test whether the declining, absorbed synchrotron comes from a dense He shell, a stellar wind, or ISM-like gas, in tension with standard Ia progenitor mass-loss channels.
papers.method: Multi-epoch JVLA 1.5–10 GHz imaging (CASA calibration, MT-MFS tclean, point-source fits with $f_p\propto\nu^{\alpha}$) builds the light curve through 1301 days. Spectra are treated as absorbed synchrotron; Appendix B adopts SSA with $\alpha_{\rm thick}=+2.5$ and MCMC spectral fits. Shell models fix $\epsilon_e=0.1$, $\epsilon_B=0.1$ and fully ionized He, $n_e=\rho/(2m_p)$, and constrain $t_{\rm end}$.
papers.reason: This is a quantitative shock–CSM synchrotron study of helium-rich SN 2020eyj, useful for circumstellar-interaction and plateau work, but it is a single Type Ia progenitor case rather than an FRB, jet, neutrino, or central-engine result.

papers.title: A 3+1 formalism for self-similar expanding grids in computational relativistic and Newtonian magnetohydrodynamics
papers.result: Fixed and SSE runs agree quantitatively on shock tubes, blasts, and jets while preserving conservation and $\partial_i\mathcal{B}^i=0$. For the spherical blast with $a(t)=(1+t/\tau)^{\kappa}$, $\kappa=0.85$, $\tau=0.55$, and $\Gamma_{\rm ad}=4/3$, the wave reaches $\bar{r}\simeq 9$ at $t=12$ after a physical-scale growth $>20$ but only $\sim 1.6$ in coordinate distance, with $T_{\rm sse}/T_{\rm fix}\sim 0.3$ and about one-third the zones of a comparable fixed mesh. In the 2D Riemann jetlet, $\Gamma_{\rm max}$ rises from $\sim 30$ to $\sim 40$; at $t=40$ the cylindrical jet ($v^z=0.99$, $a=5$) matches head, lateral expansion, and oblique shocks, having expanded $\sim 18$ times on the fixed mesh versus $\sim 3.5$ in SSE coordinates.
papers.problem: Astrophysical flows such as GRB and kilonova ejecta, supernovae and remnants, wind bubbles, pulsar-wind nebulae, and jet cocoons span large scale changes, so fixed meshes lose resolution, stretched meshes restrict the timestep and create aspect-ratio artifacts, and AMR or moving meshes make energy-momentum conservation and the divergence-free magnetic constraint difficult to maintain.
papers.method: Using only $3+1$ gauge freedom, SSE coordinates are the transformation $\bar{t}=t$, $\bar{x}^i=a_i(t)x^i$, with the linear choice $a_i=1+t/\tau$, giving $\alpha=1$, $\beta^i=(\dot{a}_i/a_i)x^i$, and $K_{ij}=0$. The conserved system remains $\partial_t\mathbf{\mathcal{U}}+\partial_j\mathbf{\mathcal{F}}^j=\mathbf{\mathcal{S}}$, with an added momentum source $(\dot{a}_i/a_i)S_i$; tests use ECHO, an ideal $\Gamma$-law, HLL, second-order MC reconstruction, and ${\rm CFL}=0.3$, without changing the mesh or solver core.
papers.reason: This is a numerical 3+1 method for self-similar expanding grids in relativistic and Newtonian MHD, directly usable for jets, supernovae, remnants, and pulsar-wind nebulae, but it does not itself deliver a new compact-source or emission result.

papers.title: Linear Electrostatic Instabilities Driven by Relativistic Non-Maxwellian Pair Beams
papers.result: For the controlled weak-beam case $p_0/(m_e c)=10$, $\sigma_\parallel/(m_e c)=0.5$, $\sigma_\perp/(m_e c)=0.1$ and $n_b/n_p=10^{-9}$, $\kappa=1.7$–$100$ and Gaussian beams all peak on the strictly parallel branch. As $\kappa$ increases, $\zeta_{\max}/\omega_{pe}$ falls from $7.51\times10^{-6}$ toward the Gaussian value $1.24\times10^{-6}$. The Maxwell–Jüttner comparison instead has its local maximum at $(K_\parallel,K_\perp)=(1.00735,0.186)$, or $\theta_{\max}=10.45^\circ$. Because the weak-beam expression is linear in beam density, $\zeta/\omega_{pe}\propto n_b/n_p$. At fixed mean momentum and RMS spreads, more extended $\kappa$ tails have higher maximum growth than a Gaussian, and the ratio approaches 1 by $\kappa=100$.
papers.problem: Relativistic electron–positron beams induced by blazar VHE emission can drive electrostatic plasma instabilities, but the linear growth depends on the beam momentum distribution; whether that growth removes beam energy before a GeV cascade develops is not settled by the linear calculation.
papers.method: Anisotropic shifted $\kappa$ distributions, their $\kappa\to\infty$ Gaussian limit, and a drifting Maxwell–Jüttner distribution are inserted into the electrostatic dielectric response of a cold unmagnetized background, $\epsilon_L(\omega,\boldsymbol{k})=1-\omega_{pe}^2/\omega^2+\chi_b=0$. In the dilute-beam limit, $\omega=\omega_r+i\zeta$ with $\omega_r\simeq\omega_{pe}$ and $|\zeta|\ll\omega_r$, giving $\zeta(\boldsymbol{k})\simeq\frac{\pi e^{2}\omega_{pe}}{2\varepsilon_0 k^{2}}\int\boldsymbol{k}\cdot\boldsymbol{\nabla}_p f_b\,\delta(\omega_{pe}-\boldsymbol{k}\cdot\boldsymbol{v})\,\mathrm{d}^3p$. Finite RMS spreads require $\kappa>3/2$, with $\sigma_\parallel^2=\kappa a_\parallel^2/(2\kappa-3)$ and $\sigma_\perp^2=\kappa a_\perp^2/(2\kappa-3)$.
papers.reason: The paper quantifies how non-Maxwellian momentum tails change the linear electrostatic growth of blazar-induced relativistic pair beams, relevant to jet secondary cascades, but it is a controlled linear test rather than a nonlinear or cosmological energy-loss calculation.

papers.title: The imprint of neutron escape on non-thermal protons in AGN coronae
papers.result: At fixed non-thermal proton energy density in a magnetized turbulent corona, neutron escape lowers the characteristic neutrino energy by up to a factor of $\sim 4$ and the integrated neutrino luminosity by $\sim 30\%$ ($\sim 35\%$ before secondary $\pi,\mu$ synchrotron cooling). In Scenario II the all-flavor peak moves from tens of TeV to below $10\,\mathrm{TeV}$ and the proton cutoff falls below $10^{5}\,\mathrm{GeV}$, more than $3\times$ below the continuous-energy-loss result. The low-energy proton density and the injection rate needed to hold $u_p$ fixed each change by nearly two orders of magnitude, consistent with $n_p^{\rm TD}/n_p^{\rm CEL}\approx\tau_{\rm esc,p}(E_p^*)\Gamma_p^{\rm int}(E_p^*)$ near $E_p^*\sim 10^{4}\,\mathrm{GeV}$. For near-ballistic magnetic reconnection the $En(E)$ peak shifts by only $\sim 20\%$, neutrons carry $\sim 25\%$ of the nucleon energy density, and the neutrino spectra are almost unchanged.
papers.problem: Continuous-energy-loss models omit the fast escape of neutrons formed by $p\gamma$ conversion. The paper asks how large that channel is for AGN coronal neutrino spectra, given the IceCube diffuse flux, its mismatch with Fermi-LAT gamma rays, and the NGC 1068 neutrino excess relative to a lower gamma-ray upper limit.
papers.method: Steady proton–neutron trickle-down transport is compared with a continuous-energy-loss Fokker–Planck treatment. The corona size and target density are $\mathcal{R}_{c}\simeq 1.5\times 10^{13}(r/10)(M/10^{7}M_{\odot})\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $n_{\rm back}=\frac{3}{4\pi\mathcal{R}_{c}^{2}c\varepsilon}\frac{dL}{d\varepsilon}$. Turbulent acceleration uses energy-independent $\tau_{\rm acc}=10\ell/(\sigma_{\rm tur}c)$ with $\tau_{\rm esc,p}\ge\mathcal{R}_{c}/c$; neutron decay reinjects protons as $Q_{p\leftarrow n}^{\rm dec}(E)\simeq n_n(E)/\tau_{\rm dec,n}(E)$. Photopion neutrinos use the Kelner & Aharonian kernel with $\eta=4\varepsilon E_p/(m_p^{2}c^{4})$. Scenario I includes coronal X-rays plus disk optical–UV photons and Scenario II only X-rays; reconnection is run only for Scenario II.
papers.reason: This work quantifies how photohadronic neutron escape changes non-thermal nucleon spectra and neutrino output in AGN coronae, which is useful for compact-object neutrino modeling such as NGC 1068, but it is not centered on FRBs, supernovae, or jets.

papers.title: Impact of the Initial Lorentz Factor on Kinetic Instabilities, Magnetic-Field Evolution, and Particle Acceleration in Relativistic Jets
papers.result: At fixed $B_0=0.5c$, jets with $\gamma_0=15$ collimate electrons more strongly, while $\gamma_0=10$ has larger linear-stage kinetic growth. Because $\sigma=B_0^2/(\mu_0 n_e m_e\gamma_0 c^2)$, the magnetizations are $\sigma=2.60\times10^{-2}$ ($\gamma_0=10$) and $\sigma=1.73\times10^{-2}$ ($\gamma_0=15$). The quoted cold-shear maximum growth rate $\Gamma_{\max}/\omega_{pe}=\beta_0/\sqrt{\gamma_0}$ decreases for $\gamma_0>\sqrt{3}$. Total-field peaks reach about $4.318$ ($\sim17.2\times$) and $12.51$ ($\sim50\times$) for $e^{\pm}$ jets at $\gamma_0=10$ and $15$, and $25.70$ ($\sim103\times$) for the $e^{-}$-$i^{+}$ jet at $\gamma_0=15$. Jet kinetic energy is transferred to electromagnetic energy and ambient particles; nonlinear-stage jet electrons ($x/\Delta>550$) reach $\gamma=20$–$38$, with $\gamma_0=15$ extending to $\gamma\approx35$–$40$. Ions at $m_i/m_e=4$ are not effectively accelerated by kKHI or MI.
papers.problem: How the injected Lorentz factor controls kinetic instabilities, toroidal-field evolution, collimation, and particle acceleration in weakly magnetized relativistic $e^{\pm}$ and $e^{-}$-$i^{+}$ jets.
papers.method: Global 3D PIC simulations with TRISTAN-MPI on a Cartesian mesh in cylindrical jet geometry compare $\gamma_0=10$ and $\gamma_0=15$ at fixed $B_0=0.5c$. The injected toroidal field is $B_\phi(r)=B_0(r/a)/[1+(r/a)^2]$ with $a=r_{jt}/2$, top-hat density $n_{jt}=8$ and $n_{\rm amb}=12$, $r_{jt}=100\Delta$, $\lambda_{se}=10\Delta$, and $m_i/m_e=4$ for ion runs; instability strength is interpreted with $\Gamma_{\max}/\omega_{pe}=\beta_0/\sqrt{\gamma_0}$.
papers.reason: The global 3D PIC comparison directly quantifies how $\gamma_0$ changes kinetic instability growth, toroidal-field amplification, and electron acceleration in relativistic jets, which is useful for jet-physics modeling even though the runs are AGN-oriented, short, and use $m_i/m_e=4$.

papers.title: No Supersoft X-rays Before SN 2026ahvu: Constraints on a Potentially Prompt Type Ia Progenitor
papers.result: Pre-explosion Chandra data (2015 and 2024; 95.3 ks) yield zero 0.3–7 keV photons in a $2''$ aperture. For a $100\,\mathrm{eV}$ blackbody and only Galactic absorption, the 95% bolometric limits are $L<6.32\times10^{37}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ at $9.1\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ and $L<2.73\times10^{38}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ at $18.9\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, excluding a hot, compact, steady hydrogen-burning white dwarf. A benchmark burner with $\dot{M}_{\rm burn}=5\times10^{-7}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$, $X=0.72$ and $\epsilon_{\rm H}=6\times10^{18}\,\mathrm{erg\,g^{-1}}$ has $L_{\rm bol}\simeq1.36\times10^{38}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. Cooler ($50\,\mathrm{eV}$) limits weaken to $<2.04\times10^{39}$ and $<8.8\times10^{39}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ at the two distances, so cooler or more absorbed photospheres remain allowed.
papers.problem: If SN 2026ahvu is a prompt Type Ia with a delay $\lesssim100\,\mathrm{Myr}$, did its progenitor have a luminous supersoft, nuclear-burning white-dwarf photosphere that Chandra should have detected before explosion?
papers.method: Two Chandra/ACIS epochs were reduced with CIAO/CALDB using a $2''$ source aperture, a $5''$–$15''$ background annulus, and observation-specific ARF/RMF with \texttt{wabs} absorption ($N_{\mathrm{H}}=7.43\times10^{19}\,\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$, plus a $10^{21}\,\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$ case). Zero counts give a one-sided 95% Poisson mean of 2.996 source counts; blackbody count-rate limits are converted to bolometric luminosity at 9.1 and 18.9 Mpc.
papers.reason: Archival Chandra limits test whether SN 2026ahvu had a hot, compact, steady hydrogen-burning white-dwarf progenitor, an incremental high-energy constraint on a compact accretor rather than a core-collapse engine or shock–CSM study.

papers.title: EP241206a: A Sub-kilosecond X-Ray Flare Possibly from an Active Galactic Nucleus with a Flux Increase over 3 Orders of Magnitude
papers.result: EP241206a is a single-peaked soft X-ray flare lasting $\sim 500\,\mathrm{s}$, with average unabsorbed flux $4.9^{+1.2}_{-1.2}\times 10^{-10}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,cm^{-2}}$ and fluence $\sim 2.5\times 10^{-7}\,\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}}$. If associated with the $z=0.62$ AGN, the persistent luminosity is $L_{2-10\,\mathrm{keV}}\simeq 2.3\times 10^{44}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ while the flare peak is $\sim 1.4\times 10^{48}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, a rise of more than three orders of magnitude. For $M_{\mathrm{BH}}\approx 3.8\times 10^{7}M_{\odot}$, the apparent Eddington ratios are $\sim 0.8$ (persistent) and $\sim 4.6\times 10^{3}$ (peak). A reconnection estimate $L_{X,\mathrm{obs}}\sim\delta_{\mathrm{eff}}^{4}\eta_{X}B^{2}cR_{\mathrm{em}}^{2}\beta_{\mathrm{rec}}/4$ gives $\sim 7\times 10^{47}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ for $\eta_{X}=0.1$, $B=10^{4}\,\mathrm{G}$, $R_{\mathrm{em}}=17R_{g}$ and $\beta_{\mathrm{rec}}\sim 0.1$. An AGN-disk long GRB would have $E_{\mathrm{iso}}=1.1_{-0.3}^{+0.4}\times 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$ at photon index $\sim 2$, off the Type II Amati relation. The WISE counterpart lies in the mid-infrared AGN region and is consistent with the blazar locus; lack of a gamma-ray flare does not rule out a temporarily beamed plasmoid.
papers.problem: The paper asks whether the sub-kilosecond soft X-ray flare EP241206a is physically associated with a $z=0.62$ AGN and whether inner-jet magnetic reconnection, a jet-in-the-jet, or a GRB embedded in the AGN disk can explain a flux increase of more than three orders of magnitude.
papers.method: WXT provides two exposures and a time-averaged Galactic-absorbed power law with $\Gamma=2.0^{+0.5}_{-0.4}$; the unabsorbed flux and fluence are measured over $\sim 500\,\mathrm{s}$. The counterpart is classified with WISE colors, optical spectroscopy, and radio flux densities, and the chance coincidence is estimated from $P_{1}=1-\exp(-\Sigma A_{\mathrm{WXT}})$. Jet origin is tested with $t_{\mathrm{obs}}\sim 30$–$3000\,\mathrm{s}$ and $L_{X,\mathrm{obs}}\sim\delta_{\mathrm{eff}}^{4}\eta_{X}B^{2}cR_{\mathrm{em}}^{2}\beta_{\mathrm{rec}}/4$, where $\eta_{X}\equiv f_{\mathrm{rec}}\epsilon_{\mathrm{rad}}f_{X}$ and $\beta_{\mathrm{rec}}\sim 0.1$.
papers.reason: This fast X-ray transient is a useful relativistic-jet and compact-object high-energy case: a ~500 s flare may be AGN-jet reconnection or an AGN-disk GRB, but the AGN association is not secure and the result is not central to FRB or supernova-engine work.

papers.title: Conditions for mass-loading: Investigating jet-disk material exchange in strongly magnetised accretion flows
papers.result: In an $a=0.9375$ MAD, eruptions recur on $\sim2000\,t_g$. Buildup, MAD, and eruption phases last $723\pm422\,t_g$, $427\pm85\,t_g$ ($\Phi_{\rm BH}>60$), and $343\pm151\,t_g$. An eruption lowers horizon flux by $\sim15\%$, $P_{\rm jet}$ by $\sim55\%$, and $\dot{M}$ by $\sim35\%$, with $\dot{M}_{\rm disk}/\dot{M}_{\rm jet}\to1.4$ and $P_{\rm jet}=\dot{M}c^{2}-\dot{E}$. Net disk flux across $\sigma=1$ is positive over $20$–$80\,r_g$, so disk plasma enters the sheath ($\sigma_{\rm sh}<\sigma<1$, $\sigma_{\rm sh}=10^{-1.8}$) but not the spine. For M87*, $t_g\approx3.2\times10^{4}\,\mathrm{s}$ implies a $\sim1$–$2\,\mathrm{yr}$ cadence.
papers.problem: Baryons must cross a strong magnetic barrier into a Poynting jet, where $\rho_{\rm disk}/\rho_{\rm jet}\sim10^{4}$, if hadronic $\gamma$-ray and neutrino emission occurs; leptonic/hadronic SEDs are degenerate, and pair-dominated reconfinement at $R_{\rm Bondi}=2GM/c_s^{2}$ is challenged by VHE and neutrino observations.
papers.method: Ideal GRMHD is evolved with H-AMR on fixed Kerr using passive tracers $D_{\rm tr}=\rho\theta_{\rm tr}$. The floor is $\rho_{\rm fl}=\max[b^{2}/(25\rho_0 c^{2}),10^{-7}\rho_0 r^{-2},10^{-20}\rho_0]$, limiting $\sigma=b^{2}/(\rho c^{2})$. Exchange is measured with $dM/d\ln\sigma$ and boundary flux $\rho\theta_{\rm tr}u_n$, where $u_n=u^{r}\partial_{r}\sigma+u^{\theta}\partial_{\theta}\sigma$ and $u_n>0$ is inflow.
papers.reason: A high-spin MAD GRMHD study shows intermittent disk-to-jet-sheath mass loading, which is useful for hadronic jet, neutrino, and VHE models, but it does not calculate radiation or neutrinos.

papers.title: X-ray Flare Evolution and Changing-Look Nature of the TeV Blazar OQ 334
papers.result: X-ray flares X1–X3 harden from $\Gamma=1.97\pm0.09$ to $1.71\pm0.04$ and $1.34\pm0.06$. FSRQ-like states are hardest ($\Gamma_X\approx1.32$–$1.52$) and BL Lac-like states softest ($\Gamma_X\approx1.77$–$2.36$); within CL states $F_{\rm X-ray}$ and $\Gamma_X$ correlate positively ($r=0.59$, $p=2.53\times10^{-2}$), i.e. softer-when-brighter, while the long-term index–flux correlation is insignificant ($r=-0.14$, $p=0.27$). The one-zone fit has nearly constant $B\approx0.11$–$0.14$, $U_{\rm e}/U_{\rm B}$ rising from 126 to 631, and $P_{\rm jet}=2\pi R_b^2\Gamma^2\beta c U_{\rm i}$ rising from $1.05\times10^{47}$ to $5.87\times10^{47}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. X-rays change from substantial synchrotron in X1 to fully inverse-Compton dominated in X3. MAGIC gives $N_0=(1.37\pm0.18)\times10^{-9}\,\mathrm{TeV^{-1}\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$ and $\Gamma=3.48\pm0.32$.
papers.problem: Whether the changing-look FSRQ/BL Lac behavior and the evolving X-ray spectrum and hysteresis of OQ 334 are produced by a variable jet synchrotron continuum diluting the broad lines, rather than by a change in magnetic-field strength.
papers.method: MAGIC (MARS/Gammapy, 50–500 GeV) intrinsic spectra are EBL-absorbed power laws; Swift-XRT (0.3–10 keV) uses Cash statistics and $\mathrm{AIC}_c$ among absorbed power-law, log-parabola, and broken power-law models with fixed $N_{\rm H}=1.08\times10^{20}\,\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$. Timing uses ZDCF, flares use Bayesian Blocks ($p_0=0.05$, $F_{BB}\ge2\times\bar F$), and SEDs use agnpy one-zone leptonic models with SSC X-rays and EC on dust-torus photons.
papers.reason: This is a relativistic-jet case study of TeV blazar OQ 334, linking X-ray hardening and changing-look states to a shift from synchrotron to inverse-Compton emission in a particle-dominated jet.

papers.title: Neural Surrogates for Tabulated Nuclear Equations of State in Core-Collapse Supernova Simulations
papers.result: Along isentropes at $Y_e=0.3$, maximum relative errors reach $6.6\%$, $14.2\%$, and $29.7\%$ for $P$, $c_s$, and $\Gamma$. Additional shock tubes keep relative $L_1$ errors below $2.5\times 10^{-3}$ in $\rho$ and $P$ and below $4.5\times 10^{-3}$ in $v$, with fiducial hydrodynamic errors $\sim 10^{-3}$. A $64\times 4$ network stores $\sim 100\,\mathrm{kB}$ versus $\sim 160\,\mathrm{MB}$ for LS220 ($\sim 1500\times$); lower validation MSE does not necessarily reduce hydrodynamic error.
